title: Hack Club
text: Hack Club is a nonprofit community where teenagers learn technology by building projects. Its current website describes Hack Club as a movement of teenagers making projects and states that its main community is for teens aged 13 to 18.

title: Hack Club Community
text: Hack Club provides a community where teenagers can explore technology, build projects, attend events, participate in clubs, and learn from other people who are interested in making things with technology.

title: Hack Club Eligibility
text: Hack Club's core programs are generally intended for students between 13 and 18 years old. Individual programs can have their own eligibility requirements, so the rules of a specific program should be checked separately.

title: Hack Club Clubs
text: Hack Club supports student-led coding clubs where students can meet, learn, build projects, and share their work. Students can find an existing club or start a club with support from Hack Club.

title: Hack Club Programs
text: Hack Club runs online and in-person programs and events focused on building technical projects. Programs can include software, hardware, hackathons, workshops, and project-based challenges.

title: Hack Club Cost
text: Hack Club states that its community is free for teenagers. Individual programs can have their own rules and requirements, but Hack Club's main community is offered without a participation fee for teens.

title: GitHub
text: GitHub is a web-based platform for hosting Git repositories and collaborating on software projects. It provides tools for storing code, reviewing changes, managing issues, and working with other developers.

title: Git
text: Git is a distributed version control system used to track changes in files and software projects. It allows developers to create commits, work with branches, compare changes, and maintain project history.

title: Git Repository
text: A Git repository contains project files together with their version history. The repository records changes through commits and can contain multiple branches for different lines of development.

title: Git Commit
text: A Git commit records a set of changes made to a project. Commits create a history that developers can inspect to understand how files changed over time.

title: Git Branch
text: A Git branch is a separate line of development within a repository. Developers can create a branch to work on a feature or change without directly changing another branch.

title: Pull Request
text: A pull request is used to propose changes to a repository and have those changes reviewed before they are merged. Developers can discuss the proposed changes, review code, and make additional commits before merging.

title: Git versus GitHub
text: Git and GitHub are different. Git is a distributed version control system, while GitHub is a platform that hosts Git repositories and provides additional tools for collaboration, code review, issues, and project management.

title: Open Source
text: Open-source software is software whose source code is made available under terms that allow people to inspect, use, modify, or distribute it according to the applicable license. GitHub hosts many open-source projects.

title: Python
text: Python is a high-level programming language known for readable syntax and a large standard library. It is used for scripting, automation, web development, data processing, scientific computing, and many other applications.

title: Python Functions
text: A function in Python is a reusable block of code that can accept inputs called parameters and can return a result. Functions help organize programs into smaller and reusable pieces.

title: Python Lists
text: A Python list is an ordered and mutable collection that can contain multiple values. Lists can contain values of different types and support operations such as indexing, slicing, adding elements, and removing elements.

title: Python Dictionaries
text: A Python dictionary stores data as key-value pairs. Dictionaries are useful when a program needs to associate a key with a corresponding value and retrieve that value efficiently.

title: Java
text: Java is a general-purpose programming language commonly used for object-oriented software development. Java source code is compiled into bytecode that can run on the Java Virtual Machine.

title: Object Oriented Programming
text: Object-oriented programming organizes software around objects that contain data and behavior. Common object-oriented concepts include classes, objects, inheritance, encapsulation, abstraction, and polymorphism.

title: JavaScript
text: JavaScript is a programming language widely used to add interactive behavior to web applications. It can run inside web browsers and can also be used in server-side and other environments.

title: JavaScript in Web Development
text: JavaScript can respond to user actions, modify web page content, communicate with servers, and control application behavior in a browser. It is commonly used together with HTML and CSS.

title: Frontend Development
text: Frontend development focuses on the part of a web application that users see and interact with. It commonly includes layouts, buttons, forms, navigation, visual components, and browser-side application behavior.

title: Backend Development
text: Backend development handles server-side application logic, data processing, authentication, database access, and responses to requests from clients such as web browsers or mobile applications.

title: HTML
text: HTML, or HyperText Markup Language, defines the structure and meaning of content on a web page. HTML elements can represent headings, paragraphs, links, images, forms, and other content.

title: CSS
text: CSS, or Cascading Style Sheets, is used to control the presentation of web documents. CSS can define layout, spacing, typography, colors, and other visual properties.

title: HTTP
text: HTTP is an application-layer protocol used for communication between clients and servers. Web browsers commonly use HTTP requests to retrieve resources and communicate with web servers.

title: HTTPS
text: HTTPS is HTTP protected using TLS encryption. It helps protect data exchanged between a client and server from being read or modified by unauthorized parties during transmission.

title: API
text: An API, or Application Programming Interface, defines how software components can communicate with each other. APIs can expose operations or data that another application can request and use.

title: REST API
text: A REST API is an HTTP-based interface commonly organized around resources. Applications can use HTTP methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE to perform different operations.

title: JSON
text: JSON, or JavaScript Object Notation, is a text format used to represent structured data. It is commonly used for exchanging data between web clients and servers.

title: Database
text: A database is a system used to store, organize, manage, and retrieve data. Applications use databases to persist information that needs to remain available after the application stops running.

title: SQL
text: SQL, or Structured Query Language, is commonly used to work with relational databases. SQL can be used to query data and perform operations such as inserting, updating, and deleting records.

title: Relational Database
text: A relational database organizes data into tables containing rows and columns. Relationships between tables can be represented using keys, and SQL can be used to query related data.
